answer: Require every identity to answer latency-bound puzzles from dispersed verifiers within a tight horizon of milliseconds. Each puzzle occupies one processor and one network path for its whole window, so a single operator running a river of fake accounts cannot answer them in parallel: every extra identity needs another real machine and another connection. The fable of free identities collapses once concurrency itself has a price, the attacker pays linearly in hardware per Sybil while an honest agent pays once, and any identity that misses its window is suspended until it re-proves itself.
